waiting.title: Say when to start building
waiting.text: Nothing is being built. One question is open: whether this app's repo goes public at its first release.

questions.q: Can a book read by the natural voices go on Audible?
questions.a: No, not as things stand. ACX says a book must be narrated by a human unless authorised, and Voices by INaudio takes AI audio only from Google Play Books, ElevenLabs and Spoken Press. Those voices can be sold on your own site, labelled as machine-made, and the app keeps them away from stores that refuse them.

questions.q: Does a clone of my own voice count as human?
questions.a: Not at Voices by INaudio: its page counts a clone of your own voice as digital narration. A voice of your own, in v1.17, is always labelled as synthesized.

Linux has no AAC encoder built in. FFmpeg's would work and its licence is allowed, but the AAC patent pool is still active, so you chose MP3 and FLAC there. Every store file works on all three systems.

questions.q: Why can't Reader's Whisper just do transcripts?
questions.a: It stops at 30 seconds, gives no times, and uses the small model. It was built for dictating a sentence. v1.8 builds on it for hours of speech with a time on every word.

questions.q: When do names come from RT Story Tracker?
questions.a: v1.11, which needs facts in Story Tracker's v3.8 and its dictionary in v3.12, which isn't built yet. A chapter can come across in v1.7, because App Link already carries that.

questions.q: Will the app upload to Audible or my podcast host?
questions.a: No. It makes the files and you send them, so it needs no store login. The episode pack in v1.12 is everything your host's upload page asks for.

questions.q: What if work stops after a release?
questions.a: Each release does a real job by itself, and a project is a folder of ordinary audio files, so nothing is stranded.

questions.q: Can I replace Google's AI audiobooks with better ones?
questions.a: That's the plan in v1.5: a complete set of files the way Google asks, marked Human narrator or Synthesized voice. Try it on one book first, because Google's help doesn't describe the swap.

questions.q: Can the app learn my voice and read the book in it?
questions.a: v1.17 makes a voice from a short reading, on your own computer, with Chatterbox, which is MIT for its code and model files. You read a consent sentence into the app first, every time, and the audio is always labelled as synthesized, so ACX won't take it.

questions.q: Can I reuse my ACX recordings elsewhere?
questions.a: Only if the title isn't on an ACX exclusive deal, which runs seven years. The app asks before exporting such a title to another store.
